dispositions.selection_rule: The thin-year rule (register Y-THIN, chosen by the owner on 23 November 2026 and amended the same night with the owner's choice B1): an item, counted by its own words, is eligible when it was printed by more than half of the newspapers that survive for its weeks, and by at least 4; the eligible items printed by every newspaper that survives for their weeks are admitted (3 in 1778), and the others are chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news, about as many stories as a standard year (a target, not a quota); one affair's items are handled as in X-1800-01; the eligible items not chosen are listed here.
dispositions.paper_counting: 1778 has 11 catalogue series, which are 8 papers (C-04): the Connecticut Courant under three catalogue numbers and the Freeman's Journal / New-Hampshire Gazette under two; the two Williamsburg Virginia Gazettes are two papers. 3 to 7 papers are in print in any three weeks, so an item needs 4 papers in almost every month (5 when its printings span weeks in which all 8 survive).

dispositions.method: The automatic families first printed in 1778 that reach 3 or more papers, long-running ones included, were split into single printed items (story_items.py --long-running, items.json: 309 items printed somewhere, 130 in 4 or more catalogue series by the finder's count), and the families of 1777 were looked for on the 1778 pages (items_from_1777.json: 36 items, one in 4 papers). Every item in 3 or more papers was compared by machine with every page (about 100 words of its text, both transcriptions); the items were joined into documents and every document that might reach the bar was counted again by about 70 words from its own opening on a reference page, with every page listed and the doubtful ones read; a sweep of passages shared word for word (seven-word sequences) by 4 or more papers found short items the families miss. 125 candidates were counted this way (outputs/story_discovery_1778/counts_1778.json). The admitted stories were searched with phrase searches over all 970 pages in both transcriptions (phrase_hits.json); every hit not in the ledger was read (recitals of the bills' titles, a second copy of the New-Jersey Gazette of 1 July, other reports naming Count d'Estaing). Each printing was checked against its page scan.

counted_item_by_item.Paper counts: Counted by their own words, 76 items of 1778 are eligible (more than half of the papers that survive for their weeks, and at least 4): 55 in 4 papers, 18 in 5, 3 in 6, none in 7. Three are printed by every paper that survives for their weeks and are admitted (the landing at Bedford, 4 of 4; Congress's resolution of 4 September, 5 of 5; the manifesto of Congress, 6 of 6). 30 more are chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news; the 33 items make 26 stories (21 single items and 5 parents holding the other 12 as sub-stories). 42 eligible items are not chosen; one turns on private persons and waits for the owner. 51 more candidates were counted and are below the bar.
counted_item_by_item.Joins made by the finder: The finder chains documents printed together or sharing formulas: the two draught bills and the commissioners' later papers through the bills' titles; the commissioners' declarations and requisition of 26 August through their titles; the lists of the thirteen states; standing notices of the New-York Gazette. Each text was counted by its own words.
